newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares post small gains, aided by dollar.
newsitem.headline: German shares post small gains, aided by dollar.

text.p: German shares were mostly unchanged at the outset of bourse dealings on Tuesday as market shrugged off early losses tied to the volatile dollar and profit-taking in DAX index heavyweight share Allianz AG.
The 30-share DAX was up 1.48 points at 4,125.67 points, while the IBIS DAX was down 16.71 points at 4,125.48 points.
Traders said the early modest losses were due to the market taking a breather after its sharp dollar-driven gains on Monday but said the uptrend appeared to be intact.
Despite the weak start, dealers said they did not expect any heavy selling pressure on the market, predicting that the DAX would trade in a range between 4,100 and 4,150 points.
"This is not a consolidation, it's a break," said one trader. "The money will keep coming in."
The dollar's brief drop from Monday's highs, caused by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel saying on Tuesday that forex markets were overreacting, was the main trigger.

But the dollar recovered to trade above 1.79 marks in morning dealings and gave renewed strength to the German share market since many DAX index components are industrial corporations strongly dependent on exports.
Declines on shares in Allianz AG and Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG in particular weighed on the market.
Both shares had shot higher on Monday, with Munich Re rising nearly seven percent in bourse trade, after it reported higher than expected earnings for the 1996/1997 business year.
Munich Re was down 25 marks at 6,325 marks while Allianz was down 4.50 marks at 428.50 marks.
Chemical shares led the gains on Tuesday as Hoechst AG surged 1.55 marks to 81.55 marks, BASF AG rose 1.10 marks to 68.65 marks and Bayer AG rose 65 pfennigs at 74.50 marks.
Carmaker Volkswagen AG, which, has been leading the DAX advance, was lower, falling five marks to 1,476 marks. Another top carmaker, Porsche AG, was down 40 marks at 2,890 marks.
But BMW AG was at a new record high, rising five marks to 1,544 marks and Daimler-Benz AG was up 50 pfennigs at 149.10 marks.
